question: Is laminate flooring a bad idea in Florida?
title: Is Laminate Flooring a Bad Idea in Florida?
h1: Is Laminate Flooring a Bad Idea in Florida Homes?
description: Sarasota's humidity averages 74% year-round. See when laminate works with the right moisture barrier and product, and when it doesn't, in 2026.
capsule: Not automatically, but it needs the right product and prep: Sarasota's outdoor humidity averages 74% year-round, and standard laminate swells if moisture reaches its core. Water-resistant laminate with a WetProtect-style warranty covers spills, pet accidents and wet mopping, but excludes flooding and standing water. Over concrete, Mohawk requires a 6-mil polyethylene moisture barrier with 8-inch overlapped seams before any laminate goes down.

sections.h2: Is Laminate Flooring a Bad Idea in Florida Homes?
sections.html:
It's not automatically a bad idea, but Florida's climate takes standard laminate off the table for a lot of rooms. Laminate's core is compressed wood fiber under a printed image layer, and that core swells and delaminates if moisture reaches it, whether from a spill, a slow leak, or humid air working through an unsealed seam. Sarasota's outdoor relative humidity averages about 74% year-round, and while an air-conditioned interior runs lower, a house that sits closed up during a summer trip can drift toward that outdoor number fast.

Water-resistant laminate changes the equation somewhat, since it uses a denser core and sealed edges to slow moisture intrusion. It still isn't the same product category as waterproof vinyl plank, and we tell clients that difference plainly rather than let the word "waterproof" on a box do the talking. The confusion between water-resistant and waterproof is genuinely the single most common misunderstanding we run into at the estimate stage for this material. We'd rather spend five minutes clearing that up before you order material than have you find out the hard way after a slow leak sits under a rug for a week.

Pergo's WetProtect warranty is a useful example of where the line sits. It covers household spills, pet accidents, and wet mopping, which handles most day-to-day life in a Florida home. It specifically excludes flooding, standing water, leaking pipes and appliance leaks, the exact events a coastal Sarasota county home is more likely to face than a house in a drier climate. That gap is worth reading closely before choosing laminate for a laundry room or a kitchen near an ice maker line, since those are precisely the rooms where a slow, undetected leak is most likely to happen over months rather than minutes. A leak under a dishwasher or an ice maker line can run for weeks before anyone notices a change underfoot, and by then a laminate floor has usually already swollen well beyond what a warranty claim will cover.

sections.h2: What It Takes to Install Laminate Over a Florida Slab
sections.html: Mohawk's laminate installation FAQ is specific here: a moisture barrier is required over concrete, and for a floating floor that means 6-mil polyethylene film with seams overlapped 8 inches. Skipping that step is one of the most common ways we see laminate fail early in this market, not because the product was defective, but because vapor coming up through an unprotected slab had nowhere else to go but into the laminate core. We also recommend a moisture test on the slab itself before ordering material, since a barrier alone doesn't compensate for a slab that's testing well outside normal range.

sections.h2: When We'd Steer You Toward Something Else
sections.html: We'll still install laminate in a Sarasota or Manatee County living room, bedroom or office with the right barrier in place. We won't recommend it for a bathroom, laundry room, or a screened lanai transition, where water-resistant simply isn't the same guarantee as waterproof. For those rooms, laminate's water-resistant cousin, vinyl plank, is usually the better call; see our comparison of waterproof laminate vs luxury vinyl plank for the full breakdown, and our laminate flooring cost guide for current pricing on the rooms where it is a good fit. Mixing materials room by room is normal in this market, and we'll lay out exactly where the line falls on your specific floor plan at the estimate.

faqs.q: Does laminate need to acclimate before installing it in Florida?
faqs.a: Most manufacturers recommend acclimating laminate in the room for 48-72 hours before installation, longer than some vinyl products, since the wood-fiber core is more moisture-reactive.

faqs.q: Can laminate go in a Florida kitchen?
faqs.a: Water-resistant laminate can, away from the sink and dishwasher gap, but we generally recommend LVP or tile in kitchens given the leak risk from appliances over time.

faqs.q: Is a moisture barrier required under all laminate, or just on concrete?
faqs.a: Manufacturers require it specifically over concrete slabs. See our post on whether you need a moisture barrier under laminate on a concrete floor for the full spec.
